title: Not by bread alone (Deuteronomy 8:1–3)
hook: the hunger in the wilderness taught them to live by every word
carry: carried, even when it didn't feel like it

segments.voice: Yesterday: ebed, and some of the hardest laws in the Bible, read without defending or skipping. Your line: read the hard parts honestly.

Four in the afternoon, and lunch never happened. First a low hum in the stomach, then a tightness, then a short answer to someone who didn't deserve it. Hunger is honest. Now stretch that to forty years of depending, morning after morning, on food that came with the dew and spoiled if it was saved. Moses, near the end of his life, looks back at those years in Deuteronomy, and says something surprising about the hunger. It wasn't an accident. It was a lesson.
screen: `FOUR O'CLOCK, NO LUNCH.` → `HUNGER IS HONEST.` → `THE HUNGER WAS A LESSON.`

segments.voice: Moses says, in the King James Bible: "thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness." And then: "he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live." Look at the order. First the hunger. Then the manna, a food nobody had ever seen, so nobody could take credit for it. Then the lesson: you need bread, yes, and you also need something bread can't give, the word that comes from God. Moses adds a tender detail in the next verse: in all those forty years, your clothes didn't wear out, and your feet didn't swell. Carried, even when it didn't feel like it. Later, in the Gospels, Jesus is alone in the wilderness for forty days, fasting, and he's hungry. The tempter says: if you're the Son of God, turn these stones into bread. Jesus answers with this verse from Deuteronomy, in slightly different words. In the King James Bible's Matthew: "Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God." Christians who keep fasts, in Lent or before communion or at other times, often reach for this verse to explain them: not to punish the body, but to let a little hunger remind them what else they live on.
screen: `REMEMBER ALL THE WAY.` · `FIRST THE HUNGER, THEN THE MANNA.` · `CLOTHES THAT DIDN'T WEAR OUT.` · `JESUS ANSWERS WITH THIS VERSE.` · then, large: `MAN SHALL NOT LIVE BY BREAD ALONE.`

segments.voice: Notice what you're hungry for beyond food: rest, attention, being known, a word from God. Some people let a small hunger, one skipped snack or dessert, be the reminder; only if it's safe for you, and if you're pregnant, unwell, or have any history with food that makes this hard, skip the hunger and keep just the listening. If you pray, turn each pang into a short prayer.
Manna. The food nobody had seen before, given each morning in the wilderness, to teach that man does not live by bread alone.
Your line: carried, even when it didn't feel like it. Even the clothes didn't wear out. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians fast at certain times, such as Lent, Fridays or before communion, and Orthodox and Catholic Christians keep set fasting days; this verse is a common way to explain why.
